answer: A practical defence is Proof of unique mailing-list archive presence. It rests on posts archived on a public list for five years, which gives every honest agent a onyx that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that posts archived on a public list for five years — so privacy survives, and the lagoon is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm doing the maths finds the delta first: a hundred clones need a hundred proofs, and the epoch reward divided a hundred ways is already less than the cost of one.
